title: A year volunteering in Guatemala
instructions: You are going to listen to a radio interview with a young woman who spent a year volunteering abroad. Answer questions 1–10 in no more than FOUR words. You will hear the recording twice. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Egy rádióinterjút hallasz egy fiatal nővel, aki egy évet önkénteskedett külföldön. Válaszolj az 1–10. kérdésre legfeljebb NÉGY szóval. A felvételt kétszer hallod; a 0. a példa.

script.speaker: I
script.text: My guest today is Kirsty Webb, a twenty-four-year-old from Brisbane who spent most of last year volunteering in a small town in the highlands of Guatemala. Kirsty, welcome. How did that come about?

script.speaker: K
script.text: Thanks. Well, it wasn't exactly planned. I'd just finished my degree in social work, and I was meant to start a job at a hospital, but the start date got pushed back by six months. A friend of mine had volunteered with a small organisation there, and she said, why don't you go? So I did. I was supposed to stay for six months, and I ended up staying for eleven.

script.speaker: I
script.text: And what did the work involve?

script.speaker: K
script.text: The organisation runs an after-school programme for kids whose parents work long hours, mostly picking coffee on the farms around the town. I helped with homework, ran a reading club, that kind of thing. But, honestly, for the first few weeks I wasn't much use at all. My Spanish was terrible. I'd done a three-week course before I left, and I thought that would be enough. It wasn't. The kids found it hilarious – they'd correct me all the time.

script.speaker: K
script.text: It was, but in a way it was the best thing that could have happened, because it turned everything upside down. I'd come thinking I was there to teach, and suddenly I was the one being taught. It made me a lot more patient – and a lot less sure of myself, which, looking back, was quite healthy.

script.speaker: I
script.text: Some people are quite critical of volunteering abroad, aren't they? They call it voluntourism.

script.speaker: K
script.text: Yeah, and a lot of that criticism is fair. There are programmes where you pay thousands of dollars to spend two weeks painting a school that was painted by the last group, and the group before that. That's more about the volunteers' photos than about the community. What I liked about our organisation was that it was run entirely by local people. The director, Rosa, used to say: we don't need you to save us, we need you to turn up on time and listen.

script.speaker: I
script.text: What was the hardest part of the year?

script.speaker: K
script.text: Strangely, it wasn't the work, or the cold showers, or even the food, although I did lose about five kilos in the first two months. It was being so far away when my grandmother got ill. I couldn't just jump on a plane – the nearest airport was a six-hour bus ride away – well, five and a half if the roads were good. I spent a lot of evenings on the phone to my mum, feeling pretty useless.

script.speaker: I
script.text: And now you're back home. Has the experience changed what you want to do?

script.speaker: K
script.text: Completely. I did take the hospital job in the end, but I've just applied for a master's in international development. And I've started volunteering here in Brisbane, at a centre that supports newly arrived migrants. A lot of them are from Latin America, so, finally, my Spanish is actually useful! I think the biggest lesson for me was that you don't have to go to the other side of the world to make a difference.

example.prompt: What had Kirsty studied at university?
example.explanation: A helyes válasz: social work (szociális munka). Kirsty azt mondja, épp befejezte a szociális munkás diplomáját.
example.evidence: I'd just finished my degree in social work

items.prompt: How long did Kirsty stay in Guatemala in the end?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: eleven months (11 hónap). Csapda: hat hónapra tervezte, de végül tizenegy hónapig maradt („ended up staying for eleven”).
items.evidence: I was supposed to stay for six months, and I ended up staying for eleven.

items.prompt: What work do most of the children's parents do?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: picking coffee (kávészedés). A szülők többsége hosszú órákat dolgozik, főleg a város körüli farmokon szednek kávét.
items.evidence: mostly picking coffee on the farms around the town

items.prompt: Why was Kirsty not very useful in the first few weeks?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: her Spanish was terrible (nagyon gyenge volt a spanyolja). A háromhetes nyelvtanfolyam nem volt elég, a gyerekek folyton kijavították.

items.prompt: Apart from becoming less sure of herself, how did the experience change Kirsty?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: she became more patient (türelmesebb lett). Azt mondja: „It made me a lot more patient” – a kérdés a másik változást (kevésbé magabiztos lett) már kizárja.
items.evidence: It made me a lot more patient

items.prompt: According to Kirsty, who mainly benefits from some short, expensive programmes?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: the volunteers (maguk az önkéntesek). Szerinte az ilyen kéthetes, drága programok inkább az önkéntesek fotóiról szólnak, mint a közösségről – vagyis inkább az önkénteseknek jók.
items.evidence: That's more about the volunteers' photos than about the community.

items.prompt: What kind of people ran the organisation Kirsty worked for?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: local people (helyiek). Kirstynek az tetszett a szervezetben, hogy teljes egészében helyi emberek vezették („run entirely by local people”).
items.evidence: it was run entirely by local people

items.prompt: Apart from listening, what did the director say volunteers needed to do?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: turn up on time (pontosan megérkezni). Rosa szerint nem megmentőkre van szükségük, hanem olyanokra, akik időben megjelennek és odafigyelnek.
items.evidence: we need you to turn up on time and listen

items.prompt: What was the hardest part of the year for Kirsty?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: being far away (from home) when her grandmother got ill – az volt a legnehezebb, hogy nagyon messze volt, amikor a nagymamája megbetegedett. Csapda: nem a munka, a hideg zuhany vagy az étel volt a legnehezebb.
items.evidence: It was being so far away when my grandmother got ill.

items.prompt: What subject has Kirsty applied to study?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: international development (nemzetközi fejlesztés). Végül elvállalta a kórházi munkát, de most jelentkezett egy mesterképzésre ebből a szakterületből.
items.evidence: I've just applied for a master's in international development

items.prompt: Who does the centre where Kirsty volunteers now help?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: newly arrived migrants (újonnan érkezett bevándorlók). Brisbane-ben egy olyan központban önkénteskedik, amely az újonnan érkezett migránsokat segíti – sokan Latin-Amerikából jönnek, így végre hasznát veszi a spanyolnak.
items.evidence: at a centre that supports newly arrived migrants
